app.name: CircuitSync
app.tagline: Group Revit electrical devices into circuits, then queue them for Revit.

auth.heading: Sign in to CircuitSync
auth.subheading: Use your work email. We send a sign-in link, or you can use a password.
auth.linkSent: Sign-in link sent to {email}. Open it on this device so the session carries over.
auth.signUpSent: Confirmation email sent to {email}. Open the link to activate the account.
auth.wrongCredentials: That email and password do not match
auth.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment, then try again.
auth.generic: Sign-in could not be completed. Check the email and password, then try again.
auth.callbackFailed: That link has expired or was already used. Ask for a new one.

projects.heading: Projects
projects.subheading: One project stands for one Revit model.
projects.emptyTitle: No projects on this account yet.
projects.emptyBody: Create one here, then bind it from the Revit add-in. You can also create it from the add-in.

project.levelsSubheading: Pick a level and a device kind to start grouping.
project.panelsUnusableReason: This panel still has no distribution system in Revit. Fill it in there, then push the model again.
project.panelsHint: Open a panel to see the circuits and devices it feeds.
project.panelEmpty: Nothing is connected to this panel yet. Circuits made directly in Revit appear once the model is pushed again.
project.unconnectedHint: Lights and receptacles that are not on any panel yet, split per plan.
project.unconnectedNone: Every light and receptacle is connected to a panel.
project.unconnectedNoPanel: {count, plural, one {# of these already has a circuit, but no panel picked yet.} other {# of these already have a circuit, but no panel picked yet.}}
project.emptyTitle: This model has never been pushed to the cloud.
project.emptyBody: Open the CircuitSync add-in in Revit, bind the document to this project, then choose “Push model to cloud”.
project.layoutsHint: Taken from Revit plan views whose names mention lighting or socket outlet.
project.layoutsSubheading: Pick a plan to start grouping.
project.noLayoutsBody: The add-in only sends plan views whose names mention lighting or socket outlet. Check the view names in Revit, then pull the model again.
project.orphanDevices: {count, plural, other {# devices appear on no plan. Usually their Revit view filters them out, or their floor has no plan yet.}}

plan.heading: {level} · {kind}
plan.selected: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing selected} one {# point selected} other {# points selected}}
plan.emptyTitle: No devices on this level yet.
plan.emptyBody: Push the model again from the add-in if the level does have devices.
plan.hint: Click a device to select it; click the same spot again to step to the one beneath. Drag across empty space to select several. Scroll to zoom, hold the middle button to pan.

connected.heading: Already connected
connected.summary: {count, plural, other {# devices}} are in a circuit and a panel
connected.empty: Nothing is connected on this plan yet. Pick some points, create a circuit, then send it to Revit.
connected.fromRevitHint: The circuit was made in Revit, not through the web

browser.heading: System browser
browser.hint: Lighting and receptacle only. Hover to highlight them on the plan.
browser.nothingLeft: Every device on this plan is in a circuit.
browser.noCircuits: No circuits on this plan yet.

wiring.heading: Wiring by room
wiring.intro: Lamps are split in an alternating checkerboard, so one switch lights the room evenly at half. Lines only join lamps on the same switch, routing around when the path would cross another switch's lamp.
wiring.runCount: {count, plural, =0 {No lines yet} other {# switch legs}}
wiring.lineStyleHint: The add-in reads this list from the model. Push the model from the add-in to fill it.
wiring.styleHint_crossing: Lamps on the same switch are joined with straight lines. In a two-column room that gives the crossing X pattern.
wiring.styleHint_orthogonal: The same split of lamps; only the line differs — vertical and horizontal with corners cut at 45°.
wiring.inferred: Inferred from the spacing between points
wiring.inferredWarning: {count, plural, other {# rooms were inferred from point spacing, because their names did not come through from Revit. Check how they were split on the plan before using them.}}
wiring.noSwitchData: The model carries no switch data yet, so grouping boundaries are still inferred from lamp spacing. Push the model again from the add-in so the count comes from the lighting devices in each room.
wiring.noRooms: No points on this plan can be wired yet.
wiring.previewOnly: Preview only. These lines are not saved and have not been sent to Revit.
wiring.noSwitchOnLayout: This plan has no switches, so grouping boundaries here are inferred from lamp spacing. If Revit does have them, check whether the Lighting Devices category is visible in this view.
wiring.sendRuns: {count, plural, =0 {Send lines to Revit} other {Send # legs to Revit}}
wiring.sendNeedsSelection: Pick points on the plan first — what gets sent is your selection, not the whole floor.
wiring.sendNeedsWholeRun: No switch leg is fully selected yet. Widen the selection until a whole leg is inside, so the lines in Revit match what you see here.
wiring.sendNeedsLineStyle: Pick a line style first; the add-in uses it as the line style in the model.
wiring.sendPartial: {count, plural, other {# legs skipped because only part of their points are selected.}}
wiring.sent: {count, plural, other {# legs queued. Fetch the plan from the add-in to draw them; the existing lines on this plan will be replaced.}}
wiring.lineStyleNeedsMigration: The line style table does not exist in the database yet. Run the latest migration (supabase db push), then push the model again from the add-in.
wiring.sendNeedsMigration: The database has no function for queueing lines yet. Run the latest migration (supabase db push), then try again.
wiring.inModel: {count, plural, other {# line segments are currently in Revit for this plan. Sending again replaces them rather than stacking on top.}}

circuits.heading: Circuits
circuits.noUsablePanel: No usable panel yet. Fill in the panel distribution system in Revit, then push the model again.
circuits.queuedNote: The add-in picks it up when the model is open in Revit.
circuits.emptyTitle: No circuits on this level yet.
circuits.editHint: This circuit’s devices are already selected on the plan. Add or remove some, then save — {number} goes back to Revit, and the number can change because Revit picks the slot.

status.no_panelHint: On a circuit, panel not chosen
status.no_connectorHint: Has no electrical connector, cannot be selected

setup.heading: Setup state
setup.subheading: This page reports what is connected and what is not. Open it from the domain that misbehaves.
setup.usingDefault: The variable name in Vercel must match this row exactly, including the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix and the capitals. Any other name (supabase_url, for example) is never read. These must also not be marked Sensitive — the value has to be inlined at build time, and it is public by design. Deploy again after fixing.
setup.authHint: The URL or key matches no Supabase project. Copy both again from Project Settings → API.
setup.schemaHint: The migration has never been run against this project. Paste supabase/migrations/20260728000000_init.sql into the Supabase SQL Editor, run it, then reload this page.
setup.schemaBlockedHint: The query never reached the database. Fix the two rows above first — once the URL, the key, and Auth are right, this row usually follows.
setup.redirectUrl: Redirect URL used by sign-in links
setup.redirectHint: This address must be listed under Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs in Supabase. Without it, sign-in links are rejected.
setup.latestMigrationHint: The devices.panel_unique_id column is missing. Run 20260729030000_device_panel.sql in the SQL Editor, then push the model again from the add-in. The app still works without it, but panel contents only cover circuits made through the web — circuits made directly in Revit stay invisible.

errors.unknown: The change was not saved. Try again.
errors.notFoundBody: The link may have changed. Go back to the project list.
errors.noAccess: That project does not belong to this account.
errors.schemaMissing: The database is not set up yet.
errors.schemaMissingBody: The tables do not exist in this Supabase project, so there is nothing to read. Run the migration first.
errors.loadFailed: The data could not be read.
errors.loadFailedBody: Supabase refused this request. Check the project URL, the key, and the RLS policies.
